items.title: Study planning is better served by Monte Carlo simulation than AI-generated participants
items.author: Jamie Cummins
items.content: ‘Silicon samples’, AI-generated synthetic data based on demographic profiles, have been proposed to help plan research. Here, I argue that Monte Carlo simulation already does this job transparently, and that generative AI is better used to help write such simulations.

items.title: Unequal causes and consequences of AI use
items.author: Yinghui Liang
items.content: Generative AI enters organizations rife with inequality. Here, we propose a recursive process whereby inequality can drive marginalized group members to use AI, but actual or suspected AI use can reinforce inequality through unequal judgement of communicators’ capability, credibility, and authenticity.

items.title: Intrinsic motivation improves performance with less effort than extrinsic motivation
items.author: Mathias Pessiglione
items.content: A new ‘different-cost’ model of effort allocation to learning under intrinsic vs. extrinsic motivation is tested across six studies combining behavioral tasks, pupillometry and computational modelling. Evidence is found in favor of the new model, showing that intrinsic motivation alleviates the effort cost attached to improving memory performance

items.title: A continuous appraisal account of gratitude dynamics in social interactions
items.author: Xiaolin Zhou
items.content: This study examines how recipients’ gratitude changes in social interactions across six experiments. Gratitude emerged after a benefactor’s decision to help and changed with help effectiveness, supporting a continuous appraisal account of gratitude

items.title: Stimulation uncertainty reveals distinct mechanisms of sensation seeking and impulsivity
items.author: Charley M. Wu
items.content: Classical accounts of sensation seeking emphasise attraction to stimulating outcomes. This study examines the complementary role of uncertainty, showing that sensation seekers seek uncertainty when stimulation value is low but avoid it when value is high, a profile distinct from impulsivity.

items.title: Effect sizes for brain-based predictive models of cognition across the lifespan
items.author: E. Dhamala
items.content: This review synthesizes literature on brain-based cognitive predictions using large-scale datasets, examining how methodological choices and data-related factors impact model performance. Key advances are proposed to improve the precision and utility of brain-based cognitive predictions.
